statement: Formula (2.3) defines a finite random variable, and Dn(bn) := n1/3 − n X a=1 la,n =⇒ D(b) jointly with the edge coordinates. Almost surely P a la = ∞. The law of (Za)a≥1 conditioned on S = D(b) has a version Π = Πg characterized by continuous conditional densities. It is independent of the admissible choice of b. Let µsp denote normalized surface measure on the sphere of radius √ n, tilted by exp(XTWX/2). The fixed-coordinate marginals of n−1/3UTX under µsp converge jointly in distribution with the eigenvalues to the random marginals of Π. On the spectral representations of Remark 2.2, this is ordinary weak convergence of measures, including convergence of every fixed polynomial moment. On the sets in Remark 2.2, for every fixed 0 ≤ j < ∞ one has Z |xa|j dΠ ≤ Cjlj/2 a , µsp |xa|j ≤ Cjlj/2 a,n, (2.4) uniformly in the retained coordinate a. For any sufficiently large fixed m, the tail (xa)a>m under Π has a density relative to N a>m N(0, la). Conditional on this tail, the first m coordinates lie on the sphere of squared radius D(b) + X a≤m la − X a>m (x2 a − la), (2.5) with the Gaussian angular density on that sphere. In particular, P a(x2 a − la) = D(b) holds Π-almost surely.
